text:
alex_chen: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we try a 'local control-plane shard' experiment for a subset of Private customers in eu-west-1. Primary goals: reduce cp latency for on-prem agents and limit blast radius during rollout. thoughts?

morgan: curious — how would agents pick a shard? sticky by region + customer ID? or registry-driven assignment?

alex_chen: plan was registry-driven: control-plane registry returns a shard endpoint on bootstrap. sticky for 24h, then re-resolve. fallback to global cp if shard unreachable.

saira: two immediate ops concerns: cert rotation across shards, and cross-shard failover preserving open sessions. If we fallback to global cp, do we rekey the agent?

alex_chen: good call. idea: shards share a signing CA (read-only) for client cert verification but rotate leaf certs per-shard. On fallback we keep session keys but re-establish long-living mTLS using the global leaf cert as a bridge.

jamie: sounds complex. What about simpler: share same intermediate CA across shards so agent certs are valid everywhere without rekey during failover? avoids rebootstrap but reduces isolation.

morgan: tradeoff: isolation vs operational simplicity. Shared intermediate CA = easier failover, but a compromise on blast radius (if CA compromised all shards impacted). We need a threat model decision.

saira: also: routing changes — if shard A goes down, switching to global cp may trigger sudden reconnect storm. We should stagger probe/backoff and have per-customer jitter.

alex_chen: agree. propose reconnection policy: jittered exponential backoff + token-bucket controlled ramp (server-side allowlist) so we can throttle reconnects per-shard. Implementation: agent uses "Retry-After" header when returning to global cp.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout created: local-cp-shard-experiment -> 5 customers in eu-west-1. canary windows: 10m ramp, 2h observation.

jamie: telemetry ask: add metrics for certificate re-auths, reconnection rate, and cp latency p50/p95 per-customer. We need an alert if reconnections spike > 5x baseline.

morgan: ops runbook snippet we should add now: 1) disable shard in registry -> 2) set shard to draining mode to serve existing sessions -> 3) enable global fallback rate limit to 10r/s/customer -> 4) monitor reconnections and cert reauths.

saira: one more: storage of shard-specific secrets. If we keep the same intermediate CA, secret sync is simpler; if not, we need secure replication (KMS-wrapped) and rotation automation. Ops prefers fewer secret sync paths.

alex_chen: decision points for RFC follow-up: 1) initially use shared intermediate CA for canary to simplify, 2) implement graceful drain + token-bucket reconnect control, 3) collect reconnection and cert metrics, 4) evaluate isolation tradeoffs before wider rollout.

morgan: +1 to canary with shared intermediate CA, but add a short-lived mitigation: pre-signed revocation list push if a shard key is suspected.

jamie: will add telemetry dashboards and an alert runbook.

alex_chen: thanks — updating the RFC follow-up doc with these decisions and the ops runbook. tagging @morgan @saira for final sign-off :memo:
